EVERY ITEM COMES FROM A REAL MERGED PR IN THIS REPOSITORY. The `symptom` is what
was actually observed before anyone knew the cause; the `cause` is what it turned
out to be. Both were written up in the PR body BEFORE this eval existed, which is
the whole point: neither was authored to make the graph look good.

competent engineer with no graph. If a task can only be answered by someone who

items.symptom: In this repo, `smart_grep` is called with `path` pointing at a single existing source file and a pattern that is definitely present in that file. It returns `{ success: true, totalMatches: 0, filesSearched: 0 }`. The same search using `files: [<that same path>]` finds the match. Diagnose the cause.
items.cause: `path` is assigned to the search root (`cwd: options.path ?? ...`) and the file list defaults to `['**/*']`; a glob rooted AT a file matches nothing, so filesSearched is 0.
wrong_turns: concluding the pattern is genuinely absent
blaming the regex or escaping
blaming caching or the ignore patterns
items.finding: smart_grep/smart_glob `path` naming a single FILE returns success with zero matches: `path` is assigned to the search root and the default glob ('**/*') cannot match with a file as cwd. Resolve a file to its parent directory plus an escaped basename.

items.symptom: A source-scanning test reports that the `condition` option of the alert_manager tool declares no nested schema at all, and lists every field of its interface as missing. Reading the file shows `condition` plainly does declare `properties` with all of those fields. Explain why the scanner is wrong.
items.cause: Array-ness was decided by testing the whole block for `type: 'array'`, which matches a NESTED array property (`groupBy`, `filters`). The scanner then reached into `groupBy.items`, which has no `properties`, and reported the option as shapeless. The type must be read at the object's own depth.
wrong_turns: editing the schema to re-add fields that are already there
concluding the schema is genuinely incomplete
assuming the brace matching is off
items.finding: In the schema source scanners, a property's `type` and `required` must be read at the object's OWN depth. A plain search over the whole block matches nested properties -- an object containing an array field was classified as an array, then read through `items`, and reported as declaring nothing.

items.symptom: A jest suite fails intermittently, roughly one run in five, on Windows. There is no assertion output and no stack trace -- the worker simply vanishes. The only output is: `Assertion failed: code_point < 0x10FFFF, file deps/uv/src/idna.c, line 397`. The suite uses property-based testing over arbitrary strings. Diagnose it.
items.cause: A native abort in libuv, not a test failure: U+10FFFF is a legal code point and libuv's assert is strictly less-than (off by one), so converting a path containing it to UTF-16 on Windows kills the process. try/catch cannot catch it. Fixed upstream in libuv 1.52.0.
wrong_turns: treating it as a flaky test and retrying or quarantining
adding a try/catch around the failing call
raising a timeout or reducing the property-test iteration count
items.finding: A path containing U+10FFFF aborts the process on Windows: libuv's assert in `uv_wtf8_to_utf16` is `code_point < 0x10FFFF`, off by one. It is a NATIVE abort, so try/catch cannot catch it, and it reaches existsSync/statSync/readFileSync alike. Guard the path before the fs call.

items.symptom: This repo publishes to npm and to the MCP registry. `package.json` is at 5.4.3, but `server.json` says 5.1.1 and `mcp.json` says 0.2.0. Every CI check is green and has been for many releases. Explain how this happened and what would break.
items.cause: release-please only bumps files listed in `extra-files`, and only plugin.json was listed. Nothing checked the others. The MCP registry validates that the declared version exists on npm, so a publish with a stale server.json version is rejected with a 422.
wrong_turns: manually editing the versions without wiring release-please (they drift again next release)
assuming a CI check exists and is broken
treating it as cosmetic
items.finding: release-please bumps ONLY what is listed in `extra-files`. Any manifest carrying a version that is not listed will drift silently every release, and for server.json that means the MCP registry rejects the publish with a 422. Wire each version field by jsonpath, including nested ones.

items.symptom: Client configs in this repo launch the server with `npx @ooples/token-optimizer-mcp@latest`. A reviewer proposes pinning the exact version instead, on supply-chain grounds. Should that change be made in this repository? Justify it from the repo's own history.
items.cause: No. A numeric pin here is a derived value release-please does not bump, and it went stale for four consecutive releases -- the plugin shipped pinning 5.3.6 against a 5.4.0 package, so users installed a server three versions behind. `@latest` is enforced by pin-mcp-version.mjs and by a test asserting every spec is exactly 'latest'.
wrong_turns: agreeing and pinning the version, reintroducing the drift
citing supply-chain risk without checking whether the repo already decided this
not noticing two gates enforce @latest
items.finding: Client configs in this repo must use `@ooples/token-optimizer-mcp@latest`, not a numeric pin. A pin is a derived value release-please does not bump; it went stale for four releases and shipped a plugin that launched a server three versions behind. Two gates enforce this.

items.symptom: A call to the smart_grep tool with no `path` argument throws `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`. When it does not throw it reports `filesSearched: 0`. Small scoped searches work fine. Diagnose the root cause.
items.cause: With no path, cwd falls back to process.cwd() -- for an MCP server that is its own launch directory, so the walk enumerated ~676,875 files. That list is then passed through a spread (`...items`), and V8 caps the number of arguments a call can take at roughly 125,000, so the spread itself throws RangeError.
wrong_turns: blaming recursion or a cyclic symlink
raising the stack size with --stack-size
assuming a bug in the glob library
treating it as an out-of-memory problem
items.finding: A spread of an unbounded array throws `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` -- V8 limits a call to roughly 125,000 arguments. Append in chunks instead of spreading. Measured here at 676,875 files after cwd fell back to process.cwd().

items.symptom: A GitHub Actions workflow is meant to repair the release PR after release-please opens it. Every run instead sits in the `action_required` state having executed nothing. The workflow file is syntactically valid and its trigger matches the event. Explain why it never executes.
items.cause: release-please opens the PR using the default GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub deliberately does not trigger workflow runs from events raised by GITHUB_TOKEN -- this prevents recursive CI. Such runs are parked in action_required. A different credential (PAT or app token), or a different triggering event, is required.
wrong_turns: debugging the YAML trigger syntax
assuming branch protection or a required approval
adding more paths/branches filters
concluding the workflow file is not on the default branch
items.finding: GitHub does not run workflows triggered by events that GITHUB_TOKEN raised; those runs sit in `action_required` having executed nothing. Anything meant to react to a release-please PR must use a different credential or a different event.
items.reclassified: Registered external-knowledge on a search that was WRONG: smart_grep silently skipped .github/ (fixed in #268). GITHUB_TOKEN appears in four workflow files in that tree, so the fact is derivable. Moves the graph’s second-best result out of the class meant to show its value.

items.symptom: Publishing this server to the MCP registry fails with HTTP 422. The npm publish itself succeeded and the package is live on npm. The registry manifest is valid JSON and passes local validation. Explain the 422.
items.cause: The MCP registry validates that the version declared in the registry manifest actually exists on npm AND that the published package carries a matching mcpName. A manifest version that has drifted from the published package version is rejected with 422.
wrong_turns: assuming an auth or token problem
re-validating the JSON schema
retrying the publish
assuming the registry is down
items.finding: The MCP registry rejects a publish with HTTP 422 when the version in the registry manifest does not exist on npm carrying a matching mcpName. Keep the manifest version in lockstep with the published package version.
